result.topic_en: The page gives the formulas and logarithmic constants of a new method for computing the shortest line (geodesic) on the spheroid, i.e. the changes in latitude, azimuth and longitude along a line of length s, with second-order correction terms.
result.transcription:
Kr. [?]

Das Resultat der neuen Methode für die
kürzeste Linie auf dem Sphaeroid ist

$A = \frac{206265(1-ee\sin\varphi^2)^{\frac{3}{2}}}{a(1-ee)}$ \quad 8.5127017 130 $- \frac{3}{2}C.\log(1-ee\sin\varphi^2)$
$B = \frac{206265\sqrt{(1-ee\sin\varphi^2)}}{a}$ \quad 8.5098272 984 $- \frac{1}{2}C.\log(1-ee\sin\varphi^2)$
$\alpha = \frac{k.10^7}{24.206265^2}$ \quad [-5.2307827.966 (-10)-]
4.6287228.053 (-10)
$\mathfrak{b} = \alpha.\frac{1-ee\sin\varphi^2}{1-ee}$ \quad [-5.2...-] {+3367+}[?] $-10$ $- C.\log(1-ee\sin\varphi^2)$
4.6315972 199 $-10$
$\gamma = \frac{\mathfrak{b}.206265^2}{aa}$ \quad [-2.6773078 080 -10-] $- 2C\log(1-ee\sin\varphi^2)$
1.6512478 167 $-10$
$\delta = \frac{\alpha(1-ee)}{(1-ee\sin\varphi^2)^2}$ \quad [-5.2279083.820 -10-] $+ 2C\log(1-ee\sin\varphi^2)$
4.6258483.907 $-10$

$I = \alpha.\partial\zeta^2$ \quad $\log(1) = I + 2II$
$II = \mathfrak{b}.\partial\lambda^2$ \quad $\log(2) = I + 2III$
$III = \gamma.\partial s^2$ \quad $\log(3) = II - III = I - IV$
$IV = \delta.\partial\varphi^2$

Proxime $I + III = II + IV$

{+mit 2518.167 [?] statt [?] Kr.+}

$\Delta\varphi = -(1)A.s.\cos\zeta$
$\Delta\zeta = -(2).B.s.\sin\zeta.\mathrm{tg}\varphi$
$\Delta\lambda = -\frac{(3).B.s.\sin\zeta}{\cos\varphi}$

Bei diesen Rechnungen sind für $\zeta$ und $\varphi$ die Mittel der
Werthe die an den beiden Punkten Statt finden zum Grunde
zulegen.
$\log a$ ...... 6,8045978 348
$\log 206265$ .... 5,3144251 332

Die Excentricität hiebei nach Walbeck {+(Nein es ist [-die-] Abplattung [?] $\frac{1}{302,68}$ benutzt Kr.)+}

methods.what: Coefficient A for the latitude change on the spheroid (meridian radius of curvature in arc seconds), with its logarithm
Coefficient B for azimuth and longitude changes (prime vertical radius in arc seconds), with its logarithm
Definitions of the auxiliary second-order correction coefficients alpha, b, gamma, delta
Second-order correction terms I-IV and the logarithmic correction factors (1), (2), (3)
Approximate relation among the correction terms
Geodesic increments in latitude, azimuth and longitude along a line of length s, computed with mid-point values (midlatitude method)
Rule to use the means of zeta and phi at the two endpoints
